name: cli-init-minimal-seed
body: Minimal init seed (no-arg `kalide init`): with no path argument, `kalide init` writes, in addition to the deck (`kalide.yaml`, `slides/`, empty `assets/`), a minimal local `templates/` directory: `library.yaml`, ONE slide template `templates/slides/hello/` (a required `title` text field, optional body; a plain layout) with a validating `example.md`, and ONE theme `default` whose `theme.css` uses only system fonts and neutral colours. Its template content is exactly that one slide template and one theme: no sections templates, no fonts, no logos, no media. The deck has one slide `slides/1-hello.md` using `hello`, and `kalide.yaml` has a title and no/`default` theme. The seed is the only template content carried by the binary; it is embedded in internal/scaffold, not internal/assets (global.constraint.no-embedded-template-assets). It is distinct from the richer demo project (demo-project). When a path argument is given instead, `kalide init <path>` does not use this seed at all: it writes no local `templates/` and no starter slide, and the external library's template names are unconstrained — a valid external library need define no template (see cli-init, external-template-library). The seed tree also carries the project-root `AGENTS.md` deck-author guide (agent-authoring), copied verbatim like every other seed file; it is text-only, not a template asset and never read by validate/render/serve/list. AC: immediately after a no-arg init, `kalide start` validates templates and deck cleanly and serves the single ""hello world"" slide.
